# Full mediation test: see if control effect on m6 disappears when m10 is included
models = {}

# Model 1: m6 ~ control
for ctrl in ['a4','a2','a5']:
    X = df[[ctrl]].values
    y = df['m6'].values
    lr = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
    models[ctrl + '_direct'] = {'slope': lr.coef_[0], 'r2': lr.score(X, y)}

# Model 2: m6 ~ control + m10 (mediation test)
for ctrl in ['a4','a2','a5']:
    X = df[[ctrl, 'm10']].values
    y = df['m6'].values
    lr = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
    indirect_effect = lr.coef_[0]  # effect of control when m10 is held constant
    print(f"\n{ctrl}:")
    print(f"  Direct effect on m6 (holding m10 constant): {indirect_effect:.3f}")
    print(f"  Total effect (original): {models[ctrl + '_direct']['slope']:.3f}")
    print(f"  Mediation by m10: direct is {indirect_effect:.3f} vs total {models[ctrl + '_direct']['slope']:.3f}")
    if abs(indirect_effect) < abs(models[ctrl + '_direct']['slope']) * 0.5:
        print(f"  -> m10 mediates much of {ctrl}'s effect on m6")
